slides.title: How a customer customises it
slides.lede: Four layers, ordered by what they cost you. The rule is: never fork to change something a layer already addresses.

slides.title: Four layers, cheapest first

items.title: Layer 0 — configuration. A JSON fragment, no rebuild.
items.text: A `bootstrap` fragment in **your own** Marketplace package, served after our defaults before sign-in. Branding, themes, the Nuxeo endpoint, session timeouts, SSO. Install the package, reload the browser, done.

items.title: Layer 1 — the manifest. Declarative, no rebuild.
items.text: A `manifest` fragment in the same package, versioned with it. Hide, reorder, relabel or rule-gate anything addressable by ID; add your own entries.

items.title: Layer 2 — your own code. An npm library you own.
items.text: `provideSatoriExtensions()` contributes slots, rules, actions and components by ID. One line in your app config. **No edits to our libraries.**

items.title: Layer 3 — the agent harness. For building the above.
items.text: Generators, a documented ID contract, and a guardrail script — so an AI agent or a new developer can extend the product without reading our source.

slides.footnote: Layers 0 and 1 need no build and no developer. Layer 2 needs a developer but no fork. Only a change none of the four addresses is a reason to talk to us.

slides.title: It survives your next upgrade — rehearsed
slides.lede: The marketplace installer copies our bundle directory with `overwrite="true"`, and installs **no** configuration file. Your fragments live in your own package, which depends on ours, so upgrading ours cannot replace them. Rehearsed with `nuxeoctl mp-install`: upgrading ours with two customer packages installed served byte-identical configuration (NXSAT-312).

blocks.code: // agentic-ui-config/bootstrap.json in YOUR configuration package // — a fragment contributed to org.nuxeo.agentic.ui.config { "branding": { "applicationTitle": "Acme Content", "documentTitle": "Acme Content" }, "defaultThemeId": "acme", "themes": [{ "id": "acme", "label": "Acme", "base": "nuxeo", "tokens": { "--mat-sys-primary": "#1f6feb", "--mat-sys-surface": "#ffffff" } }], "nuxeoApiOrigin": "" }

slides.footnote: Every key is optional. A key no package sets falls back to the value compiled in — so a server with only our package behaves exactly like no configuration at all. `AppConfigService.diagnostics()` reports which half loaded and which fell back, and why. The product's tokens are the `--mat-sys-*` Material system properties; `base` names the compiled palette they layer over. An earlier cut of this slide showed `--shell-nav-*`, which only the forkable template defines — in the product those keys apply and nothing reads them.

slides.title: Change the interface without changing the build
slides.lede: Everything addressable has an ID of the form `<owner>.<surface>.<name>`. The manifest names IDs; it never names a class.

blocks.code: // agentic-ui-config/manifest.json in YOUR configuration package { "extensions": { "overrides": { "app.navbar.trash": { "visible": false }, // hide it "app.navbar.assets": { "label": "Documents" }, // rename it "app.navbar.dashboard": { "order": 5 } // move it }, "slots": { "navbar": [{ "id": "acme.navbar.contracts", "label": "Contracts", "path": "/browse/contracts", "icon": "folder", "order": 35, "rule": "acme.rules.isLegalTeam" // gate it on your own rule }] } } }

slides.footnote: An **unregistered rule ID evaluates to `true`** on purpose, so a typo or a manifest written against a newer release cannot silently strip working actions out of the UI. The exception is rules that gate administrative surfaces — those are declared fail-closed.

slides.title: Thirteen slots. Seven carry ours; six are empty and live.

panels.title: Populated — ours is in it, and you can change ours
panels.sub: Packaged descriptors exist and the surface renders from them — 7 of 13

panels.title: Resolves — live, but nothing of ours is in it
panels.sub: Contribute here and it takes effect; there is just nothing to override — 6 of 13, with one exception below
items: `documentMetadata`, `documentEdit` — **a component of yours** in place of the Properties panel or the Edit dialog form
**`documentCreate` is the exception** — it resolves, but no product screen opens the create form yet, so a contribution has no visible effect today

slides.footnote: `docs/extension-reference.md` marks each slot _populated_, _resolves_ or _reserved and inert_, and those are three different promises. **No slot is reserved-and-inert today** — an earlier cut of this slide said five of them were, and that was still being shown after they went live. But _resolves_ is not the same as _usable_: `documentCreate` resolves into a create form no screen opens (`extension-reference.md:245`), so it is the one slot where contributing changes nothing a user sees. **And note what these three slots take: a component, not a list of fields.** Choosing which *fields* a type shows is a per-type **layout file**, which is not a slot and has no id (§9b); these slots put a component of yours where that layout would have rendered, for when a list of fields cannot express what the type needs (§9c). Read the reference rather than this slide if the two disagree.

slides.title: One function. Four registries. No fork.
slides.lede: Generate the library, write your contributions, add one line to your app config. Our libraries are untouched.

blocks.code: $ npx nx g @nuxeo-satori/generators:extension-library acme-extensions --owner=acme // src/lib/extensions.ts — everything you contribute, in one object provideSatoriExtensions(() => { const rules = inject(AcmeRulesService); // yes, you can inject return { slots: { navbar: NAV_ITEMS }, rules: { 'acme.rules.canUseAcme': (ctx) => rules.canUse(ctx) }, failClosedRules: ['acme.rules.canUseAcme'], components: { 'acme.panel.reports': () => import('./panel').then(m => m.Panel) }, actions: { 'acme.actions.export': { execute: (ctx) => rules.export(ctx) } }, }; });

slides.footnote: The generator also emits **six specs that assert the IDs are really registered** — because a library that registers descriptors nothing renders is the failure this whole contract exists to prevent.

slides.title: Hiding a control is not a security control

blocks.text: Layer 1 decides what the interface **offers**. Nuxeo decides what the server **allows**, server-side, on every operation. Hiding `app.toolbar.delete` does not stop a user with `Remove` from deleting via the REST API, and showing it grants nothing. Use Nuxeo ACLs for authorisation; use the manifest for what the interface presents.

slides.footnote: `failClosedRules` closes a startup-timing gap in the *interface* — the window before registration completes, where an unknown rule would otherwise fail open. It is not authorisation either.

slides.title: An upgrade is a version bump
slides.lede: That claim is only true if none of your customisation lives inside our code — which is what the four layers are for.
